test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In ΔABC if ∠A = 50° and ∠B = 70°, find the measure of exterior angle A.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Exterior angle at any vertex of a triangle is the **sum of the two opposite interior angles**.

Exterior ∠A = ∠B + ∠C

First find ∠C = 180° − (50° + 70°) = 60°.

Exterior ∠A = 70° + 60° = 130°.

**∴ The correct answer is 130°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠A = 50°, ∠B = 70°

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles on a straight line is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e07a3d7b61f1ad6d57b0a6da5545b5531c6c40242792a8f6692a4e40d6bae97f.png] 

In ΔABC, interior **∠A = 50°**.

The interior angle and the exterior angle at the same vertex form a **linear pair**.

⇒ Interior ∠A + Exterior ∠A = 180°

⇒ 50° + Exterior ∠A = 180°

⇒ Exterior ∠A = 180° − 50°

⇒ Exterior ∠A = 130°

**∴ The correct answer is 130°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles.

Linear Pair Postulate

If two angles form a linear pair, then they are supplementary, meaning their sum is exactly 180°.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of any triangle is always 180° (∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°).</p
